Subject (in full) Case against Waung Maung Nung (汪夢農) and Wong Tse Ping
(王紫萍) charged with being communists.
Made by D.I. Kuh Pao-hwa. Forwarded by [签名]

Regarding the case against Waung Maung Nung (汪夢農)
alias Wong San (王三) and Wong Tse Ping (female 王紫萍) who
were arrested on the authority of a warrant issued at the request
of the Chinese Authorities, at 11.30 p.m. March 22, 1935 at No. 53
Seymour Road, on a charge of being communists, which was concluded
on March 27 when both accused were ordered to be extradited to the
Chinese Authorities, I forward herewith tabulated statements
referring to these two individuals, a list of the literature seized,
together with a draft of a covering letter to the French Police
relating to this case.

Kuh Pao-hwa
D. I.

D. C. (Special Branch).

SECOND BRANCH KIANGSU HIGH COURT A.M.

Mr. Kum appeared for the S. M. Council.
Mr. Tseu Kuh Ying for both accused.

Proceedings. Wit. Dung Pau:- I am the representative of the Public
Safety Bureau. On the 26.3.35, a despatch was received from
the Chekiang Peace Preservation Corps, for the handing over of
the accused. (despatch produced). The statements made by Ying
Tsung Liang were also forwarded from Chekiang (produced). I also
have the letters which were previously received (produced).
1st. accused:- I know Ying Tsung Liang, but I did not
ask him to organize a Anti Japanese Group.
Mr. Kum:- When the accused were arrested two letters
and five books were seized. The letters were subjected to
chemical treatment, and one of them shows secret communistic
literature. (produced)
Mr. Tseu:- Here is the testimony of Messrs Langdon's
showing that the accused is of good character (produced).
1st. accused:- (on being shown the statement made by
Ying Tsung Liang) Parts of the statement made by Ying are not
true. When he came to Shanghai, he asked me where he could
address letters to me, and I gave him the firm Post Office Box No,
1241. One day my old school mate gave me a paper in which a
number of persons proposed organising an Anti Japanese Group, and
amongst the names was that of Madame Sung Ching Ling. I sent the
paper to Ying Tsung Liang, but did not add anything to it. I have
often seen articles in the paper about this group made by Madame
Sung Ching Ling.
Mr. Kum:- Police have no objection to the handing over of
the accused.

SUMMING UP.

诉讼程序。证人董保 (Dung Pau)：- 我是公安局代表。1935年3月26日，收到浙江保安团发来的一份公文，要求移交被告。（出示公文）。应宗良 (Ying Tsung Liang) 所作的供词也由浙江方面转发过来（出示）。我还持有此前收到的信件（出示）。
第一被告：- 我认识应宗良，但我没有让他组织抗日团体。
金先生：- 被告被捕时，查获两封信和五本书。信件经过化学处理，其中一封显示有秘密共产主义文献。（出示）
徐先生：- 这是兰登先生 (Messrs Langdon) 的证明，表明被告品行良好（出示）。
第一被告：- （在看应宗良的供词时）应的一部分供词不属实。当他来到上海时，他问我哪里可以给我写信，我给了他公司的邮政信箱1241号。有一天，我的老同学给我一张纸，上面有许多人提议组织一个抗日团体，其中的名字包括宋庆龄女士。我把这张纸寄给了应宗良，但没有添加任何内容。我经常在报纸上看到关于宋庆龄女士组建的这个团体的文章。
金先生：- 警方对移交被告无异议。

总结陈词。

Application is hereby made for the detention of the above

activities and were arrested at 11.30 p.m 22/3/35 at 53 Seymour
Road on the authority of S.S.D. Court Warrant of Arrest issued

Proceedings
Mr. King S Kum appeared for the S.M.C.

1st accused :- I am an accountant of the Hon Chong Co. at
Rue Cardinal Mercier, French Town.

Mr Kum :- These two accused are communists suspects who
were arrested at the request of the Shanghai Public Safety Bureau,
armed with warrants No. 6252/596, 6253/2410 came to Bubbling Well
Police Station ask for assistance in effecting the arrest of the
two accused. Detectives went with him to 53 Seymour Road where
these two accused were arrested and the two letters and five books
were also seized (produced). The representative of the B road
stated that they have received two letters from the Chekiang Peace
Preservation Corps asking them to arrest the two accused. These
are the statements made by the two accused at the station (produced)

Representative Young Pau, S.P.S.Bureau :- On 6/12/34 we
received a letter from the Chekiang Peace Preservation Corps stating
that one named Ying Tseng Lien, who was arrested by them, has im-
plicated the accused who were supposed to work in the Hon Chong Co.,
Yates Road. We went there and could not find such a firm there.
On the 4th inst. we received another letter stating that the accused
were living at Rue Cardinal Mercier but upon information received
from private agent we learned that the accused were living at 53
Seymour Road. Consequently we applied for the warrants and with the
assistance of the Municipal Police we arrested the two accused and
seized the books and letters there. We ask the case be remanded

第一被告：- 我是法租界梅神父路宏昌公司 (Hon Chong Co.) 的会计。

金先生：- 这两名被告是共产党嫌疑人，是应上海市公安局的请求被捕的。警方持第6252/596号和6253/2410号逮捕令来到静安寺捕房，请求协助逮捕这两名被告。侦探随他前往西摩路53号，在那里逮捕了这两名被告，并查获了两封信和五本书（出示）。B路（原文如此，疑指某部门或道路代号）的代表称，他们收到浙江保安团的两封信，要求逮捕这两名被告。这是两名被告在警局所作的供词（出示）

Tuan Fu (端甫),
(Secret letter No.3) March 18.

I have received the letters dated February 15 and March 9
(during this period I left this place on certain affairs so I have
just received the letter dated February 15). I sent a letter
on the 12th inst. (to Loh Han (洛亨) -Secret letter No.2) As
I have just received your letter of the 13th I again communicate
the contents of that letter to you.

(A) Rebels have now left this place. Tsz Hsien (滋县) in
Hunan Province is as peaceful as ever. In accordance with my
last request to you, please send the articles as well as the newly
published papers and books without further delay.

(B) Please stop despatching anything from, or to, the place
(at Chen An 成安) where Waung Dah Ming 王大名 used to despatch his
articles, because something has happened there. (Remarks) -
Owing to the approach of the year-end, no present was sent to the
recipient and consequently deliveries were refused acceptance;
place was not raided (according to recent investigations).

(C) In order to avoid any possible setback from the hands
of enemies, our idea is to concentrate all correspondence and
to give you the main point. What is your opinion?

(D) I request that once every ten days an ordinary letter
be exchanged among us in order to safeguard our relations.

(E) Please continue using our temporary communication address
at Ngao Dee's (敖弟).

(3) Kyung Chong (景忠) did not send any letter to Hung Jao
(洪肇). This name was not mentioned in any of the previous
letters. This was undoubtedly the work of enemies. In your last
communication you used the secret code by adding 7 square - producing
the significance of 49 - then the original "Tien" (天) code
would be 1131. When we notify Tien (天), 7 square will be
added - making 49 - which will be equivalent to 1180.

(5) The four family names were given in the letter of the 1st

Translation of Exhibit No. 7 (original letter) in the case
against Waung Maung Nang (汪夢農 ) and Wong Tse Ping (王紫萍 )
arrested at 53, Seymour Road on March 22, 1935.

Dear Chih Fu ( 哲甫 ),

I have not corresponded with you for a long time,
and have not been in a position to see you owing to the
great distance that exists between us. I am thinking of
you very much.

There is nothing extraordinary happening to the
family. As the shop made no profit last year only little
assistance was given to the family; but fortunately the
harvest of cotton was good and the year passed off safely.
At present we are in poor circumstances and can hardly maintain
ourselves. Ten days ago, Shing Wen ( 兴文 ) and Tseng Hwa
( 振華 ) proceeded to Wuhu and the family gave them more
than $50. The business of the shop during the spring time
proved no better, and therefore you are requested to do
your utmost to remit home a certain part of your income.

The object of Shing Wen's departure to Wuhu is to
secure employment with the Kiangnan Railway Co. ( 江南鐵路公司 )
as the railroad is to be repaired and extended this year up
to Kiangsi. They plan to find Yoh Chung ( 耀宗 ) who will
be asked to find employment for them. I did not intend
to send Tseng Hwa, but owing to the fact that the family is
small and family affairs can be managed by one man, he set
out of his own accord.

All members of the family are very well and Wen
Sung ( 文生 ) and his brother have been sent to school.
Little Tien Sung ( 小天生 ) has been running here and there
on the street all day long. Don't worry.

With best regards,

Kwang Ming ( 光明 )
March 18, 1935.

1935年3月22日在西摩路53号被捕的汪夢農（Waung Maung Nang）和王紫萍（Wong Tse Ping）案件中，展品第7号（原信）的译文。

亲爱的哲甫（Chih Fu），

许久未与你通信，也因彼此相距甚远而未能见面。我非常想念你。

家中并无特别之事发生。由于店铺去年无利可图，对家庭的资助甚少；但幸运的是棉花收成良好，这一年平安度过。目前我们境况贫寒，难以维持生计。十天前，兴文（Shing Wen）和振華（Tseng Hwa）前往芜湖，家里给了他们50多元。春季店铺生意并无起色，因此请你尽力汇回家中部分收入。

兴文前往芜湖的目的是为了在江南鐵路公司谋职，因为铁路今年将修缮并延伸至江西。他们计划寻找耀宗（Yoh Chung），请他为他们找工作。我本无意派遣振華，但由于家口简单，家事一人即可打理，他便自行出发。

全家成员均安好，文生（Wen Sung）及其兄弟已送入学校。小天生（Little Tien Sung）整天在街上跑来跑去。请勿挂念。

致以最良好的祝愿，

光明（Kwang Ming）
1935年3月18日。

Wang Maung Bung (汪夢農)
Ningpo                                      D. I. Everest
B'Wall Station        22-3-35.

My name is Wang Maung Bung, I am age 25 and I was born in
Ningpo. I was educated at the Hangchow Christian College and
I can read and write English. I left college in the summer of
1931 and returned to Ningpo where I obtained employment as a
teacher in the Junior Middle School of the Ningpo Methodist
College. I came to Shanghai in September, 1933, to take up a
position as book-keeper with E.W. Langdon and Co., Importers of
Machinery, Tools and Supplies, 30, Rue Cardinal Mercier, at
$45 a month. I am still employed by this firm. In February,
1934, I was married to Wong Sz Ping in Shanghai. She is a
native of Ningpo and I knew her for many years before our marriage.

I am not a communist and I have no connection with any
radical party. The three copies of the "Moscow News" and
the booklets entitled "Culture and Life in the U.S.S.R." and
Leningrad and Moscow* which were found in my room, I bought
at the American Book and Supply Co., Szechuen Road. Some of
the pro-communist books in the Chinese language I bought from
a Japanese bookshop in North Szechuen Road and others were
given to me by friends. I believe that all persons should
be free to read any literature they choose and the fact that
these books were found in my possession does not brand me
as a communist. My wife is not a communist. She does not read
my books and she has no knowledge of their contents.

I have lived at my present address in Seymour Road since
the 16th March, 1935, and previous to then with relatives in
an alleyway off Rue de Consulate.

The two unopened letters which I threw out of the motor

汪梦农 (Wang Maung Bung)
宁波                                      D. I. Everest
北四川路捕房        1935年3月22日。

我叫汪梦农，现年25岁，出生于宁波。我就读于杭州之江大学，能读写英文。我于1931年夏大学毕业，返回宁波，在宁波卫理公会中学初中部受聘为教师。我于1933年9月来到上海，在位于梅神父路30号的机械、工具及用品进口商 E.W. Langdon & Co. 公司担任簿记员，月薪45元。我目前仍受雇于该公司。1934年2月，我在上海与黄淑平 (Wong Sz Ping) 结婚。她是宁波人，我们在婚前相识多年。

我不是共产党员，与任何激进政党也没有联系。在我房间里发现的三份《莫斯科新闻》以及题为《苏联的文化与生活》和《列宁格勒与莫斯科*》的小册子，是我在四川路的美国图书文具公司购买的。部分中文亲共书籍是我在北四川路的一家日本书店购买的，其余则是朋友赠送的。我认为所有人都应有权自由阅读他们选择的任何文献，这些书在我处被发现这一事实并不能给我贴上共产党员的标签。我的妻子不是共产党员。她不读我的书，也不了解书的内容。

我自1935年3月16日起居住在西摩路目前的地址，此前则与亲戚住在领事馆路 (Rue de Consulate) 旁的一条弄堂里。

car on the way to the Police Station after my arrest are
addressed to friends care of my business address. My

ing the letters until they returned. The post office box

汪梦农 - 第2页。

我被捕后在前往警局的汽车上扔出的两封未拆封信件，是寄给我商业地址转交朋友的。我的朋友目前不在上海，我一直保管着这些信件直到他们回来。邮政信箱号码 (1241) 是由我的雇主 Langdon & Co. 租赁的，我将其用于通信。我处理掉这些信件是因为担心它们可能会连累我的朋友。
    除了申明我的清白外，我无话可说。我绝对不是共产党员，我想不出当局为何要逮捕我。
    这是我的真实陈述。
                    (签名) 汪梦农 (Waung Maung Hung)。

Wong Tae Ping.
Ningpo                                D.P.S. Duke
Bubbling Well        22/3/38.

My name is Wang Tae Ping. I am 19 years of age(foreign
reckoning) and I was born in Ningpo. When I was 9 years
old I went to the Primary School in my native place where
I remained until I was 15 years old. I then entered the
Ming Juang Middle School in Ningpo. I left this school
in 1933 at the age of 17 and came to Shanghai and studied
at the College of Fine Arts, Rue du Marche, French Concession,
for six months. In February, 1934, I married Wang Kang
Hung, whom I had met at the Chinese Y.M.C.A. in Ningpo
a little while prior to leaving Ningpo. At this time my
husband was already employed in E.F.Langdon & Company
where he is still working. After my marriage, I lived
with my husband at No.261 Rue Ratard until October 1934
when we moved to No. 1 Yah Poh Li, Shachaikwan Road in
order to live with my elder sister. In December 1934, we
moved to 12, Dah Chi g King Li, Rue Hue, owing to my sister's
husband returning from Hongkong. On the 16th of this
month(March) we moved to our present address owing to the
arrival in Shanghai from Ningpo of my mother and there
being insufficient accomodation at the old address. I
know hardly any English at all. I am not in the least
interested in Communism, and, knowing very little about it,
I cannot understand it and therefore distrust it, if
anything. I never discuss politics or world affairs with
my husband. I do not take any interest in the literature
that my husband brings home and never read them.

Signed. Wang Tae Ping.

王泰平 (Wong Tae Ping)。
宁波                                D.P.S. Duke
静安寺捕房        1938年3月22日。

我叫王泰平。现年19岁（虚岁），出生于宁波。9岁时，我在家乡进入小学就读，直至15岁。随后我进入宁波明强中学。1933年，我17岁时离开该校来到上海，在法租界市场路 (Rue du Marche) 的美术专科学校学习了六个月。1934年2月，我与王康宏 (Wang Kang Hung) 结婚，我是在离开宁波前不久在宁波中华基督教青年会认识他的。当时我的丈夫已经在 E.F. Langdon & Company 任职，至今仍在那里工作。婚后，我与丈夫住在辣塔德路 (Rue Ratard) 261号，直到1934年10月，为了与我姐姐同住，我们搬到了沙家湾路亚波里1号。1934年12月，由于姐夫从香港回来，我们搬到了霞飞路 (Rue Hue) 大奇京里 (Dah Chi g King Li) 12号。本月（3月）16日，由于我母亲从宁波来到上海，且旧住址住宿空间不足，我们搬到了现在的地址。我几乎不懂英语。我对共产主义毫无兴趣，而且知之甚少，无法理解，因此如果说有什么态度的话，我是不信任它的。我从不与丈夫讨论政治或世界事务。我对丈夫带回家的文学读物不感兴趣，也从不阅读。

签名。王泰平 (Wang Tae Ping)。
